sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc-Lko:48064
Court No. - 11
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 4998 of 2022

Applicant :- Ajeet S/O Harishchandra Rajput
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Lko. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Atul Verma,Akhilendra Pratap Singh,Alok Kumar Srivastava,Asha S
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Neeraj Sahu
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
None has appeared for the complainant.

2. The FIR in question was lodged against the applicant alleging that the applicant was staying with her aunt and on 09.12.2021 at about 1 AM, the applicant came and committed the offence under Section 376 IPC.

Subsequently, this statement was reiterated in the statements under Section 161 &
164 Cr.P.C.
Ajeet S/O Harishchandra Rajput vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Lko.

And 3 ... on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85322269/
1 3.
Learned counsel for the applicant places reliance on the examination and the cross-examination of the witness which have taken place before the trial Court.
In the cross-examination, the victim admitted that on seeing the applicant, she did not raise any alarm.
She also stated that she had not seen the applicant coming in the room.
She also stated that the applicant was lying with her for a period of two minutes.
The medical report on record does not support the prosecution story as no injury is seen in the medical report, which is on record as Annexure - 5.
It is argued that as many as 10 witnesses are proposed to be examined and only one witness has been examined so far.
The applicant is in custody since 12.12.2021 and has no criminal antecedent.

3. Learned AGA opposes the bail application by arguing that the offence is serious in nature and in the medical report, the age of the victim is 17 years, thus, the bail application should be rejected.

4. Considering the statement of the victim during the course of the trial, especially in the cross-examination coupled with the fact that the medical report does not support the prosecution story and the fact that there is no likelihood of the trial being concluded in near future, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant Ajeet be released on bail in FIR No.695 of 2021, under Section 452, 376, 504,
506 IPC & Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, P.S. Saandi, District Hardoi on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 21.7.2023 nishant  Ajeet S/O Harishchandra Rajput vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Lko.
